title: Runtime Dimensional Content Review Web
goal: Create a new internal Next.js review application that reads RTQ paper TOML and canonical maths assets directly from the active rtq-content checkout.
Allow reviewers to browse paper collections and refine a selected paper at runtime using the five dimensional tag axes without generating a new Markdown view.

Retain the established question and answer review-outcome workflow through review-api and Google Sheets, while storing append-only, RAG-state-specific comments in a versioned rtq-review SQLite database through Drizzle and never editing paper content.
Give the maintained reviewers unambiguous names by renaming the existing generated-Markdown application to review-markdown-web and naming the new direct-content application review-content-web.

in: A new application at apps/review-content-web inside the rtq-review pnpm workspace, implemented with the Next.js App Router, React, and TypeScript.

Rename the existing apps/review-web application to apps/review-markdown-web, including its package identity, workspace commands, documentation, and maintained configuration references, without changing its generated-Markdown behavior.
Read-only discovery of supported paper-level TOML collections in the configured rtq-content checkout, including canonical, focus, topic, RAG, combined focus/topic/RAG, and exemplar collections.

A file browser derived from the useful review-tag-web browsing patterns, with folder selection, paper search, focus-group/topic/RAG metadata filters where those properties exist, and direct navigation to a selected TOML file.
Runtime parsing of the selected TOML file into sections and complete question, subquestion, and sub-subquestion trees, including original-source provenance for derived papers.

Structured rendering of question text, formulas, tips, workings, answers, PaperTable, PaperImage, generated and manual working assets, LongDivision, project macros, and KaTeX without an intermediate generated Markdown file.
Rendered-content and raw-source presentation modes comparable to the useful review-web and review-question-viewer-web review views.
Resolution and display of explicit, inherited, and implicit/default dimensional tags for family, math, frame, marker, and reasoning.
Runtime filtering inside the selected paper using dimensional tag facets and result counts, with filters represented in the URL so a focused review view can be bookmarked or shared.
Question-side and answer-side review outcomes through a same-origin Next.js adapter to the existing review-api service.

Question-side and answer-side comments persisted through Drizzle in the versioned SQLite database at <rtq-review>/database/review-content.sqlite, keyed to each question, subquestion, or sub-subquestion by its own UUID (and its own question ID when present), review side, and the corresponding top-level RAG state.

Current-state comment presentation by default plus a Show everything toggle for historical prior-state comments, including author/reviewer identity and server-recorded creation time, with no edit, reset, or delete action.
Source freshness while a paper is open, clear loading/empty/error/stale states, keyboard- and screen-reader-usable controls, and responsive paper navigation.
A tested read-only paper model boundary that can be adopted by existing review applications later without requiring their migration in this iteration.

Register the primary review-content-web in the rtq-content-owned tmux YAML on port 3001, move review-markdown-web to port 3004, and move docs-web to port 3005 so all maintained review services start together.
Workspace scripts, application documentation, and proportionate unit, integration, browser-smoke, type, lint, format, and production-build validation.
out: Changing the behavior of review-markdown-web, review-tag-web, review-question-viewer-web, docs-web, or review-legacy-gatsby-web beyond the explicitly required rename, command/reference updates, and tmux port assignment.
Using review-legacy-gatsby-web as an implementation or design basis.
Editing canonical or derived TOML, tags, answers, workings, assets, or any other rtq-content source from the new application.
Replacing the existing review-api or Google Sheets review-outcome persistence workflow.
Sending new review comments to review-api or Google Sheets, or automatically importing historical Google Sheets/TOML comments into SQLite.
Changing the dimensional tag taxonomy, migration rules, style guides, or source TOML tag values.
Removing generated Markdown or derived TOML workflows that remain useful to existing applications and authoring processes.
Providing a corpus-wide virtual-paper query across every canonical paper in the initial iteration; the initial runtime dimensional filter operates within one selected paper-level TOML document.
Supporting questionNodeToml as a paper browser in the initial iteration; it is a nested one-node artifact collection rather than a paper-level collection.
Adding public deployment, authentication, authorization, or multi-tenant behavior to this internal local-review tool.
Inventing human-readable expansions or new transition semantics for the existing opaque peer-review outcome codes.
Adding paper-level peer-review mutations, for which the current review API has no companion outcome endpoint.
constraints: Canonical complete paper content remains owned by rtq-content/packages/papers/papers/toml; generated TOML collections are read-only projections and generated Markdown is not an input to the new app.
All filesystem reads must resolve through @rtq/review-repository-paths and remain contained inside the validated @rtq/papers and @rtq/maths-assets roots.

The browser must never receive arbitrary filesystem paths, private asset metadata, generated LongDivision sources, review API credentials, OAuth tokens, UUID index contents, workbook IDs, or Google Sheets rows.
Review-outcome submissions update Google Sheets only; canonical TOML changes later through the existing synchronization cycle and must not be implied to have changed immediately.

SQLite access remains server-only, all application reads and writes use Drizzle rather than hand-written SQL, and the database resides at database/review-content.sqlite under the stable rtq-review workspace root independently of RTQ_CONTENT_ROOT.
The main database is intentionally tracked with rtq-review so feedback can be read on other machines; only SQLite journal, WAL, and SHM sidecars are ignored.

Every node uses its own rtq-uuid as its required comment identity and its own rtq-question-id only when present; no top-level question ID or UUID is inherited or persisted for a nested comment. A nested node inherits only the corresponding normalized source RAG state (rtq-question-rag or rtq-answer-rag) from its containing top-level question. Comments from other RAG states are immutable history and appear only when Show everything is enabled.

App Router only; default to Server Components for filesystem reads and initial rendering data, and introduce Client Components only around interactive filtering, preferences, navigation, and review forms.
Interactive state crossing the Server Component boundary must be plain serializable data.
Use the Node.js runtime for filesystem and asset routes; do not use the Edge runtime.
Follow application AGENTS.md requirements, current Next.js 16 async request APIs, semantic styling conventions, kebab-case filenames, and repository formatting/lint/type conventions.
Do not modify user-owned changes in the legacy Gatsby generated content tree or any unrelated dirty-worktree paths.
The new application may selectively adapt existing code, but must not import private implementation modules across application directories or create a third untested copy of the TOML/tag/asset model.
The existing generated-Markdown reviewer must retain its routes, inputs, review actions, and runtime behavior after its directory/package/display-name rename.

The coordinated review stack must reserve port 3001 for the primary review-content-web, port 3004 for review-markdown-web, and port 3005 for docs-web; existing review service ports otherwise remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Rename the Markdown reviewer and establish the new application boundaries
tasks.description: Rename the existing generated-Markdown reviewer for clarity, then create the new Next.js application and a small workspace-owned read-only paper-model package so filesystem parsing, identity, tags, and filtering have one tested boundary rather than being copied wholesale from another private application.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing apps/review-web directory is renamed to apps/review-markdown-web, its package and human-facing identities use review-markdown-web/Review Markdown Web consistently, and all workspace commands and maintained references target the renamed app.

The renamed review-markdown-web retains the same generated-Markdown inputs, routes, UI, and review behavior; its service-port reassignment is limited to the T7 stack integration, and its existing checks pass after the rename.

A new App Router application exists at apps/review-content-web with package name rtq-review-content-web, display name Review Content Web, and local port 3001 without changing another existing application's behavior.
A workspace package exposes only the read-only paper collection, normalized paper tree, effective-tag, and filter contracts needed by the new app; it exports no TOML write operation.
The package builds on @rtq/review-repository-paths and does not import source files from review-tag-web or review-question-viewer-web across application boundaries.
The application defaults to Server Components and the initial server-to-client paper payload is serializable.
Root workspace scripts can start and validate the new application independently.
Tests prove that the package API cannot resolve a content path outside the validated rtq-content paper roots and that no source-write API is exposed.
tasks.notes: Implemented on 2026-09-05. The generated-Markdown app is renamed to apps/review-markdown-web with package identity rtq-review-markdown-web, maintained documentation references and root commands are updated, and its routes and runtime implementation remain unchanged. The new apps/review-content-web foundation uses package identity rtq-review-content-web. It was originally exercised on a temporary port during T1; the later T7 revision assigns primary Review Content Web to 3001, Review Markdown Web to 3004, and Docs Web to 3005. @rtq/review-paper-model exports serializable read-model contracts plus containment-checked read-only path resolution and no source-write API. Root format, lint, types, and tests pass; both app production builds pass; Docs format/lint/types/tests pass; and a runtime smoke test returned HTTP 200 with the active rtq-content checkout connected. The legacy localStorage key rtq-review-web:display-preferences is intentionally retained as a compatibility implementation detail so the rename does not reset reviewer preferences. Existing apps are intentionally not migrated to the model package in this PRD.

tasks.title: Discover and parse reviewable TOML collections read-only
tasks.description: Adapt the proven collection browser, safe path resolution, strict/loose TOML parsing, provenance, macro, working-collection, and review-metadata concepts into a normalized paper read model.
acceptanceCriteria: The collection registry covers toml, allTopicsToml, focusToml, focusTopicToml, focusRagToml, focusRagTopicToml, topicToml, ragToml, ragTopicToml, and discovered exemplarsLevel<Tier>Toml folders that exist in the configured checkout.
Missing or empty registered folders do not break other collections, and non-paper folders, manifests, hidden files, and non-TOML files are excluded.
The browser exposes file title, collection identity, question count, focus group, topic, RAG grouping, and source provenance when each value can be established without guessing.

A selected valid file is parsed into paper metadata, sections, and ordered question trees through sub-subquestion depth while preserving UUIDs, rtq-question-id provenance, raw content, content RAG, review RAG, legacy source comment metadata, and version hash.
Canonical and normal generated TOML use strict parsing; supported exemplar placeholders use the established constrained loose-read fallback without weakening ordinary-file validation.

The model resolves project abbreviations/macros, repeated formula and tip children, PaperTable, PaperImage, and LongDivision preparation inputs without exposing private asset sidecars or generated sources.
All collections are read-only in this application regardless of whether review-tag-web currently treats a folder as editable.
Unit tests cover canonical, derived, exemplar, malformed, missing, empty, traversal, provenance, repeated-working-child, and representative nested-question cases.
tasks.notes: Implemented on 2026-09-05 in @rtq/review-paper-model. The read-only boundary discovers the registered paper-level collections plus existing exemplarsLevel<Tier>Toml directories, isolates malformed files in the source index, and rejects unsupported collections such as questionNodeToml. A 2026-09-06 correction replaces the mistaken allTagsToml registration with the canonical allTopicsToml one-way projection. Selected papers parse into serializable metadata, provenance, ordered sections, and complete question/subquestion/sub-subquestion trees with stable canonical source-question IDs, UUIDs, explicit tags, source/review RAG, legacy comments, raw content, macro-expanded content, repeated formula/tip children, answers, and safe PaperTable/PaperImage/LongDivision preparation descriptors. Strict TOML remains mandatory outside recognized exemplar placeholder documents. Fixture tests cover registry ordering, missing/empty collections, excluded files/folders, canonical/derived/exemplar metadata, topic/RAG grouping, provenance, malformed input, constrained loose parsing, traversal, nesting, repeated working children, review metadata, macros, and safe preparation contexts. Workspace lint, format, types, and tests pass.

tasks.title: Implement effective dimensional tags and runtime faceted filtering
tasks.description: Resolve the five-dimensional tag model for every question node and provide immediate, URL-addressable filters over the selected paper.
acceptanceCriteria: Every node exposes stored explicit tags, inherited tags, and effective tags with their source identified as explicit, inherited, or implicit.
Family, math, frame, and reasoning inherit independently from the nearest enabled ancestor when absent locally; an explicit child value replaces only its own dimension.
A child marker set replaces rather than adds to inherited markers when markers are explicit locally, and rtq-inherit-tags=false disables inherited values.
Missing stored dimensions are interpreted at runtime as family.unknown, math.unknown, frame.raw, no markers, and reasoning.direct without writing those values into TOML.
The selected paper exposes five named facet groups populated from its effective node tags, including currently selected zero-result values long enough for the user to remove them.
Selections are combined with AND semantics between dimensions and OR semantics within one dimension, using exact tag values in the initial implementation.
A top-level question tree is included when any node in that tree satisfies the complete filter expression; the complete tree remains visible for context and matching nodes are visibly identified.

Facet counts are recalculated against the current selections in the other dimensions, zero-result choices are disabled or clearly marked, and the interface shows total and matching question-tree counts.
Filter state uses stable repeated URL search parameters for family, math, frame, marker, and reasoning; reload, back/forward navigation, bookmarks, and copied links preserve the view.
Clearing one dimension and clearing all filters are available without re-reading or regenerating Markdown or TOML.

Pure unit tests cover each inheritance rule, implicit defaults, mixed legacy/dimensional data, exact matching, AND/OR behavior, descendant matches, counts, no-result filters, URL encoding, and deterministic ordering.
tasks.notes: Implemented on 2026-09-05 in @rtq/review-paper-model. Every parsed node now exposes source explicit tags, inherited dimensional candidates with their originating ancestor node, and effective explicit/inherited/implicit tags. Family, math, frame, and reasoning resolve independently; explicit child values replace only their dimension; explicit child marker sets replace inherited markers; rtq-inherit-tags=false cuts off all ancestry; and missing dimensions receive the documented runtime-only defaults while legacy tags remain source metadata. The pure filter boundary normalizes exact tag selections, applies OR within an axis and AND across axes to the same node, returns complete matching top-level trees plus exact matching-node IDs, produces cross-filtered facet counts in stable five-axis order, retains selected zero-result values, and reports total/matching tree counts. URL helpers parse and serialize stable repeated parameters while preserving unrelated query state, with clear-one and clear-all operations. Thirteen package tests cover lineage, independent overrides, marker replacement, inheritance cutoff, implicit defaults, legacy tags, exact matching, same-node descendant matching, complete-tree retention, AND/OR behavior, cross-counts, disabled/selected zero results, deterministic ordering, URL round trips, and clearing. Workspace lint, format, types, tests, and diff checks pass. A live topic-paper smoke test reduced 25 trees to 13 complete trees/17 matching nodes for family.age plus frame.algebra and round-tripped that filter alongside view=raw. The visual controls and browser-history binding consume this tested interface in T4.

tasks.title: Build the full-paper runtime review presentation
tasks.description: Present the selected TOML document as a structured and readable bulk-review page while preserving the source detail needed to diagnose content problems.
acceptanceCriteria: The home route provides the agreed collection/file browser and a selected file route uses a stable collection plus source-relative slug.

The file page renders paper metadata, section boundaries, top-level question numbering, nested labels, UUID/source provenance, content RAG states, dimensional tags, question text, formulas, tips, workings, and answers.
KaTeX, project macros, GFM tables/PaperTable, PaperImage, manual working/answer images, and LongDivision render from canonical @rtq/maths-assets inputs through allowlisted same-origin routes.
Raw source for question, formula, tip, working, option, key, and answer values is available through a display preference without replacing the normal rendered view.
Reviewers can independently show or hide raw source, workings/answers, tags, and review controls, and preferences persist locally without altering a shared URL unless they affect review scope.

The runtime lens provides separate question-content RAG-state and answer-content RAG-state facets in addition to dimensional tags; selections combine with the existing filter semantics, remain encoded in the URL across refreshes, and the single reset action clears every tag and state filter.

Previous/next matching question navigation, top/bottom navigation, section context, active-question indication, and an empty filtered-result state support bulk review without rendering a generated HTML document.
No edit control, server action, route handler, or client request can mutate TOML or canonical assets.
Component and browser-smoke tests cover representative nested content, hidden/visible display modes, keyboard operation, empty content, filtered navigation, and asset rendering.
tasks.notes: Implemented on 2026-09-06 in review-content-web, with @rtq/review-paper-model exposing a client-safe filter subpath and per-field canonical asset context. The home route now browses all discovered live TOML collections, searches within a collection, isolates invalid papers, and links to stable /papers/<collection>/<source-relative-path> routes. Selected papers render metadata, sections, complete three-level question trees, UUID/source provenance, effective tag origins, question/answer RAG and synchronized review outcome metadata, question text, repeated formulas and tips, workings, options, keys, and answers. The client applies exact five-axis filters immediately with the native History API, retains URL-shareable scope, highlights exact matching nodes while preserving their complete top-level tree context, and provides section links, active-question state, top/bottom previous-next controls, J/K and Alt+Arrow keyboard navigation, and a zero-result state. Versioned local preferences independently control solutions, tags, raw source, and the read-only review panel; raw values supplement rather than replace rendered content. Server preparation expands project macros, normalizes PaperTable to GFM, renders KaTeX, strips authoring-only MDX comments, and resolves PaperImage plus generated LongDivision references. A GET-only same-origin route allowlists canonical question images, manual working/answer images, generated working/answer LongDivision SVGs, and the standard missing image while rejecting arbitrary asset paths; no content mutation surface exists. Unit tests cover routes/preferences/navigation, PaperTable handling, and asset containment. The committed live browser-route smoke checks the index, nested labels, display controls, positive two-axis filtering (26 to 4 matching trees), retained zero-result filters, canonical assets, and LongDivision; a representative paper also rendered 256 KaTeX expressions and six GFM tables. The 2026-09-06 filter revision adds independently cross-filtered question-content and answer-content RAG facets, compact reviewer labels, repeated question-rag and answer-rag URL parameters, selected zero-result retention, and a single complete-lens reset; model tests cover independent and combined state matching, tag/state composition, facet counts, URL round trips, and reset, while the live smoke proves a question PR plus answer not-started paper reduction from 26 trees to one. Workspace lint, format, types, and all tests pass, the live route smoke passes, and the Next.js production build succeeds. Next emits one non-fatal NFT trace warning for the intentionally runtime-resolved sibling asset checkout; no content files are bundled or written. Review outcome and append-only comment actions remain explicitly deferred to T5.

tasks.title: Add Google Sheets outcomes and local append-only review comments
tasks.description: Provide structured review controls for visible question trees. Persist review outcomes through review-api to Google Sheets, but persist comments locally in SQLite through Drizzle so feedback is durable, append-only, and associated with the exact question, subquestion, or sub-subquestion UUID, review side, and inherited top-level RAG state in which it was written.
acceptanceCriteria: Each eligible top-level question displays separate question-side and answer-side source RAG, current synchronized review outcome, locally stored comments for the current RAG state, and the target sheet code used only for outcome submission; every eligible nested node displays its own contextual question-side and answer-side comment controls without gaining a Google Sheets outcome control.
The UI supports every review outcome currently accepted by review-api—PRCC, PRPCC, PRG, PRG2, PRCR, PRPCR, PRCS, PRRL, PRR, PRA, PRBD, and PRCT—without inventing expansions or transition behavior.

Outcome requests use a Node-runtime same-origin Next.js adapter that allowlists question and answer outcome actions, validates UUID, sheet, outcome, and reviewer fields, forwards only required fields to review-api, and returns upstream status and safe errors without exposing secrets or workbook data.

Outcome controls are disabled with a clear reason when UUID or sheet routing metadata is unavailable; success is labelled as submitted to Google Sheets rather than saved to TOML, and a local pending override prevents the page from falsely showing the old value during the current view.

A Drizzle schema and committed migrations create an append-only comments table with a generated comment ID, idempotent submission ID, optional node-owned rtq-question-id, required node-owned rtq-uuid, side constrained to question or answer, normalized inherited top-level source RAG state, comment text, reviewer identity, and server-generated UTC creation timestamp; the UUID, side, state, and chronological query path is indexed without making that combination unique because multiple comments are allowed.

The application resolves the SQLite database as database/review-content.sqlite under the stable rtq-review workspace root independently of the configured rtq-content checkout, creates the database directory when needed, and fails with a clear recoverable error when the database cannot be opened or migrated.
The main database is tracked in rtq-review while its SQLite journal/WAL/SHM sidecars are narrowly ignored; an automated check proves both boundaries.

Comment listing is performed server-side and batched for the visible paper identities rather than issuing one database query per question; no database path, SQL detail, or unrelated comment record reaches the browser.

A reviewer can append a nonblank question-side or answer-side comment to a question, subquestion, or sub-subquestion when that exact node has rtq-uuid and its containing top-level question has the corresponding current source RAG state; the node's own rtq-question-id is retained when present but never inherited, and the server recursively resolves the node and verifies its UUID plus inherited top-level state against the selected read model rather than trusting arbitrary client routing fields.

Submitting a comment never calls review-api or Google Sheets, creates exactly one immutable SQLite record through Drizzle, and returns the stored ID, reviewer, side, RAG state, and creation time needed to render it immediately without a page reload.

Comments matching the exact node-owned UUID, optional node-owned question ID, side, and inherited current top-level RAG state are shown chronologically as read-only contextual feedback against that exact node after initial load and immediately after submission, including reviewer and date/time.

Current-state comments are the default presentation. A page-level Show everything toggle reveals comments for the same node identity and side at prior or otherwise nonmatching RAG states, labelled with their recorded state; turning it off hides that immutable history again.

The new application exposes no comment edit, reset, or delete operation in its UI, route handlers, Drizzle repository, or public module API; legacy review-api comment/reset endpoints and existing applications remain unchanged.
Filtering and navigating does not discard pending overrides during the current page session, and duplicate submissions are prevented while a request is active.
No legacy subtag mutation is exposed because dimensional filtering is not tag editing.

Tests use a temporary SQLite database and a mocked upstream service to cover schema migration, durable reloads, top-level/subquestion/sub-subquestion UUID isolation, optional non-inherited question IDs, inherited top-level question/answer RAG states, current-only and Show everything presentation, chronological multi-comment display, immediate append feedback, invalid or spoofed identities, blank comments, idempotent retry behavior without preventing distinct comments, database failures, absence of edit/delete/reset paths, the question/answer outcome endpoint map, every allowed outcome, missing routing metadata, upstream failures, success feedback, preservation of pending UI state, and formulas/tips rendering before workings.
tasks.notes: Implemented and revised on 2026-09-06 in review-content-web. Top-level questions retain independent question/answer Google Sheets outcome controls for all 12 review-api outcomes. Comments use a separate POST-only adapter that never calls review-api. Every question, subquestion, and sub-subquestion now has contextual question-side and answer-side comment controls keyed by that node's own required UUID and its own optional rtq-question-id; no parent ID or UUID is inherited or persisted. Recursive server verification locates the exact node in live TOML and derives only the corresponding question or answer RAG state from its containing top-level question. Current-state feedback renders against the exact node by default, and the page-level Show everything toggle reveals labelled, immutable other-state history. Initial loading recursively collects all node identities and performs one batched Drizzle query. A generated forward migration preserves existing comments, makes rtq-question-id nullable, and indexes UUID, optional question ID, side, RAG state, and chronology. The repository remains append/list/close only, with no edit, reset, or delete route. Formula and tip fields now render before their associated working. On 2026-09-07 the database path moved to the tracked <rtq-review>/database/review-content.sqlite file so feedback is distributed for read-only use on other machines; only transient SQLite sidecars remain ignored. Tests cover migrations, durable reload, nullable identity isolation, recursive sub-subquestion resolution, inherited question/answer RAG, chronological history, immediate append feedback, idempotency, validation/spoofing, safe failures, all outcomes, and duplicate suppression. Cross-reload outcomes still depend on the existing Sheets-to-canonical synchronization cycle. The existing runtime sibling-path NFT trace warning remains non-fatal.

tasks.title: Support the canonical equationNumber macro across maintained reviewers
tasks.description: Add the rtq-content KaTeX macro \equationNumber to every maintained Next.js review website before content migration begins, preserving its canonical semantic class in both display and inline mathematics without broadly trusting arbitrary KaTeX HTML extensions.
acceptanceCriteria: review-markdown-web, review-tag-web, review-question-viewer-web, and review-content-web all render \equationNumber{n} in display and inline mathematics as a footnote-sized parenthesized number with the rtq-maths-equation-number semantic class, matching rtq-content/packages/papers/new-scripts/papers/rtq-katex-macro-contract.json.

The four maintained reviewers consume one workspace-owned, client-safe equation-number KaTeX options boundary rather than adding four new divergent macro/trust definitions or importing private modules from another application.
The KaTeX trust policy permits only the canonical rtq-maths-equation-number htmlClass extension added by this task and does not enable arbitrary htmlClass, htmlStyle, URL, or other trusted commands.

Existing reviewer-specific macro behavior remains unchanged; the task does not rewrite content, generated Markdown, TOML, the canonical rtq-content macro contract, or the explicitly excluded legacy Gatsby reviewer.

Automated tests compare the shared definition with the canonical JSON contract, render representative aligned display equations and inline references, assert the semantic class and visible parenthesized number, and prove an unapproved HTML extension remains untrusted.
All four maintained reviewer applications pass their format, lint, type, test, and production-build checks after adopting the shared options boundary.
tasks.notes: Implemented on 2026-09-06 as an approved priority detour after T5. The new client-safe @rtq/review-katex-options workspace package owns the exact canonical equationNumber expansion plus a narrow trust callback that accepts only htmlClass with rtq-maths-equation-number; each maintained reviewer merges this addition with its unchanged local macro table. review-markdown-web, review-tag-web, review-question-viewer-web, and review-content-web now pass the shared options through their KaTeX render path. Shared tests compare the definition with the rtq-content JSON contract, exercise aligned display and inline rendering, assert the footnote-size class and visible parenthesized numbers, preserve a caller macro, and reject unapproved htmlClass and htmlStyle trust contexts. Each app also has a renderer-wiring test. All four apps pass format, lint, types, full unit tests (75 total), and production builds; the shared package passes format, types, and 3 contract/security tests. Existing non-fatal Turbopack sibling-path trace warnings remain unchanged. The legacy Gatsby reviewer and rtq-content sources were not changed. After acceptance, execution returns to the original T6 and T7 sequence.

tasks.title: Keep runtime content current and responsive
tasks.description: Ensure direct filesystem consumption remains useful during active authoring without repeatedly parsing the entire paper corpus or hiding source changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Initial collection and selected-paper reads occur directly on the server with no internal HTTP round trip and no generated Markdown dependency.

Opening or refreshing a paper reads its current filesystem version; an open page detects a selected-file version change and offers or performs a controlled refresh without polling and reparsing every collection file.
The browser index does not fully hydrate every paper body merely to show a file list and has a documented invalidation strategy for additions, removals, renames, and metadata changes.
Applying dimensional filters to an already loaded paper is immediate and does not trigger a server parse or Google Sheets request.

Malformed or transiently replaced source files, unavailable sibling repositories, missing assets, stale URLs, review-api outages, and unavailable or unmigrated local comment databases have specific recoverable states rather than crashing the whole application.
Development and production behavior for live source changes is documented accurately.
Integration tests cover direct source freshness, selected-file change detection, index invalidation, and recovery from a temporarily unreadable source.
tasks.notes: Implemented on 2026-09-06. Initial index and selected-paper rendering remain direct Node-runtime Server Component reads with no generated Markdown or internal HTTP round trip, while dimensional and question/answer RAG filtering remains a client-side operation over the loaded paper. @rtq/review-paper-model now retains only source summaries in a process-local cache keyed by validated collection root, file name, and filesystem fingerprint; every index request still enumerates current directories, prunes removals, discovers additions and renames, and reparses only new or changed files. Invalid summaries are deliberately not cached so transient parse failures recover on the next refresh. Selected paper reads remain uncached. A new inspectPaperSource boundary and no-store /api/papers/source-version route inspect only the open TOML file. ReviewSurface checks that endpoint on window focus or visibility restoration without polling, keeps the existing rendered paper available, distinguishes changed, temporarily invalid, unavailable, and failed-check states, and offers controlled router.refresh, retry, or index navigation. The component is keyed by collection, path, and content hash so a successful refresh reloads comments and review data while URL-backed filters and local display preferences survive. The README documents first-load cache construction, additions/removals/renames/metadata invalidation, per-process development/production behavior, and the fact that filters make no source or Sheets requests. Tests cover unchanged cache reuse, metadata edits, additions, renames, removals, direct content-hash freshness, temporary invalid TOML and recovery, deletion, freshness-state evaluation, safe URL encoding, and the endpoint's live success/no-store and unsafe-path behavior. Workspace format, lint, types, and 62 tests pass; the production build passes with the existing non-fatal sibling-path trace warning. A live smoke against Review Content Web on isolated port 3010 passed because docs-web still occupies 3004 until T7 performs the planned port move. A live 2,550-file audit confirmed the second in-process index call reused every unchanged summary.

tasks.title: Document, integrate, and validate the maintained review stack
tasks.description: Make the renamed and new applications understandable and independently runnable, then update the rtq-content-owned tmux stack so every maintained review service starts with an explicit non-conflicting port.
acceptanceCriteria: The root README and new application README explain purpose, source-of-truth boundaries, supported collections, filtering semantics, Google Sheets outcome synchronization, the versioned <rtq-review>/database/review-content.sqlite persistence location, environment/path configuration, local URL, and checks.

The root package exposes correctly named start commands for review-markdown-web and review-content-web, updates stale review-web command references, and retains compatibility aliases only if they are documented and useful.

The rtq-content-owned tmux YAML starts the primary review-content-web on port 3001, moves review-markdown-web to port 3004, starts docs-web on port 3005, and starts the other maintained review services on their existing assigned ports.

Starting the tmux stack brings up all configured services together, and HTTP smoke checks confirm that review-content-web responds on 3001, review-markdown-web responds on 3004, and docs-web responds on 3005 without a port collision.
The review-markdown-web rename and docs-web port move do not alter either application's functional behavior or generated inputs.
The new package and app pass format, lint, types, unit/integration tests, browser smoke checks, and a production build.

A manual acceptance walkthrough demonstrates choosing a canonical or derived paper, applying at least two dimensional filters, reviewing the reduced question set, opening raw source, rendering representative assets, submitting a mocked or approved non-production outcome, appending and reloading a local current-state comment, observing a prior-state comment as historical, and clearing/restoring the URL-backed filter state.
tasks.notes: Port assignment revised and implemented on 2026-09-06: review-content-web is the primary reviewer on 3001, review-markdown-web is on 3004, docs-web is on 3005, and the existing tag and question-viewer assignments remain 3002 and 3003. Root format, lint, types, and tests passed; the full review-content-web check and production build passed; review-markdown-web and docs-web production builds passed; the rtq-content repository naming audit passed. The six-window tmux stack started without a port collision, stack smoke checks passed for 3001/3004/3005, Content Web's browser smoke passed on 3001, and the other three services returned HTTP 200. No production Google Sheets write was performed. Accepted and marked done by the user on 2026-09-06.

tasks.title: Replace paper display controls with simple toggles
tasks.description: Simplify the paper-level display controls in Review Content Web so each binary choice is immediately recognizable and usable as an ordinary on/off toggle. Raw source is already supported; the gap is the custom presentation of the controls, not missing raw-working data.
acceptanceCriteria: The display controls near the start of a selected paper use a familiar, visually unambiguous switch treatment with a clear on/off state rather than the current bespoke indicator UI.

Workings & answers, Tags, and Raw source each retain their existing independent behavior and are presented as simple labelled toggles; other binary controls in the same display group use the same convention for consistency.
Every toggle remains keyboard operable, has an accessible programmatic label and checked state, and has a visible focus treatment.
Changing the visual control does not change the existing defaults, machine-local preference persistence, rendered/raw content, filtering, review state, or source TOML.
The controls remain usable and legible at narrow and wide viewport sizes without obscuring the start of the paper.

Component tests verify the accessible checked states and retained preference behavior, and the browser smoke verifies that the simple toggles visibly show and hide representative workings, tags, and raw source.
tasks.notes: First follow-up gap reported during user acceptance on 2026-09-06. The user confirmed that Raw source is already present and corrected the earlier interpretation that a separate raw-working capability was missing. Implemented on 2026-09-06 with conventional labelled switches, native checkbox semantics, visible focus styling, retained defaults, and machine-local persistence. Static interface tests cover the accessible switch contract and the production route smoke passes; final visual acceptance remains with the user.

tasks.title: Control question and answer review panels independently
tasks.description: Replace the single Review panel visibility choice with independent question-review and answer-review visibility so a reviewer can use an answer-only layout for the common workflow while keeping question review available when needed.
acceptanceCriteria: The paper-level display controls provide separate, clearly labelled Question review and Answer review toggles using the simple toggle treatment defined by T8.

The reviewer can select all four useful layouts across the complete paper: both panels, question only, answer only, or neither; answer only does not leave an empty question-panel container or unused layout space.

Each visibility choice applies consistently to the corresponding outcome controls, current-state feedback, historical feedback, and append-comment form at top-level question, subquestion, and sub-subquestion depth.
Hiding either panel is presentation-only: it does not delete comments, clear unsaved state in the other visible panel, submit an outcome, change filters, or modify source TOML.

Question-panel and answer-panel preferences persist independently in machine-local browser storage and remain outside the shareable filter URL. Existing stored single-panel preferences migrate predictably, with visible mapping to both visible and hidden mapping to both hidden.
Show previous feedback continues to control current-state versus historical feedback for whichever review side is visible, and revealing a previously hidden side restores its applicable feedback.

Tests cover all four visibility combinations, stored-preference migration and persistence, and representative nested feedback; the browser smoke verifies the answer-only layout and restoration of both panels.
tasks.notes: Second follow-up gap reported during user acceptance on 2026-09-06. Implemented on 2026-09-06 with independent Question review and Answer review preferences, all four visibility layouts, no empty hidden-side container, and deterministic migration from the former combined preference. Unit tests cover migration and every visibility combination; final visual acceptance remains with the user.

tasks.title: Lighten the review theme and increase typography
tasks.description: Make Review Content Web comfortable for sustained review by replacing near-dark content surfaces with a light neutral palette and increasing the undersized typography used for tags, paper names, metadata, controls, raw source, and other reviewer-facing information.
acceptanceCriteria: Raw-source blocks and other content-panel backgrounds no longer use near-black or strongly dark fills; differentiation uses light gray, a slightly deeper version of the main paper background, subtle borders, or similarly light neutral treatment.
The lighter surfaces retain clear hierarchy and readable foreground contrast without changing the semantic meaning of RAG, warning, success, or active-control states.

The application typography scale is increased across the paper browser and selected-paper view, including paper names, tags, metadata, filters, display controls, raw source, identifiers, review panels, comments, and navigation.

Reviewer-facing labels, tags, paper names, controls, metadata, and raw-source text are not rendered below 0.875rem at supported viewport sizes, while primary question and answer content remains at least 1rem unless a larger existing size already applies.
Increased text sizes wrap or reflow cleanly at narrow and wide viewport sizes without clipping, overlapping, truncating essential information, or creating unusable controls.
Foreground and background combinations meet WCAG AA contrast for ordinary text and interactive states, including raw-source blocks and tag badges.

Style or browser tests cover the light raw-source treatment and minimum typography scale, followed by visual verification of the paper list and a representative nested paper at desktop and narrow viewport widths.
tasks.notes: Third follow-up gap reported during user acceptance on 2026-09-06. Implemented on 2026-09-06 with a light neutral page, filter, collection, review, and raw-source palette; reviewer-facing explicit rem sizes are at least 0.875rem and primary content remains at least 1rem. Static style-contract tests guard the palette and minimum typography scale; final desktop and narrow visual acceptance remains with the user.

tasks.title: Make review feedback prominent and stable
tasks.description: Restructure feedback presentation so existing review comments are the most prominent information in each question context, historical feedback is easy to discover, and appending feedback does not continually move the Add Comment interaction down the page.
acceptanceCriteria: When a question, subquestion, or sub-subquestion has feedback, that feedback is visually dominant within the node context through stronger weight, the larger typography established by T10, and an accessible destructive/red treatment rather than a quiet neutral card.

Feedback is presented in a central or full-width region instead of being constrained to the narrow side-by-side question and answer control columns; its exact node and review side remain unmistakable.

Question and answer feedback continue to respect the independently visible review sides introduced by T9, while comments remain attached to the exact nested-node UUID and inherited top-level RAG state already stored in SQLite.

The comment composer and Add Comment action occupy a stable, predictable position. Appending one or many comments does not push the composer progressively farther down; the growing append-only history is placed after the composer, in a bounded region, or in another layout that preserves access to the action.

The vague Show everything control is replaced or supplemented by an explicit Show previous feedback control located with the feedback experience. It remains discoverable when there is only current feedback or no historical feedback and communicates current and historical counts or an equally clear empty state.

By default only feedback for the current RAG state is shown. Enabling Show previous feedback reveals immutable comments from all earlier states with their original RAG state, reviewer, and date clearly identified; disabling it returns to the current-state view.
The destructive feedback treatment remains compatible with T10's light theme, meets WCAG AA contrast, and is distinguishable from transient submission errors and success messages.

Tests cover current-only and historical visibility, zero-history discoverability, question-versus-answer context, append order, and preserved exact-node/RAG filtering. Browser verification confirms prominent feedback and a stable Add Comment position before and after appending multiple mocked comments at desktop and narrow widths.
tasks.notes: Fourth follow-up gap reported during user acceptance on 2026-09-06. Implemented on 2026-09-06 with full-width stacked review scopes, a stable composer before the growing feedback list, prominent destructive/red populated-feedback treatment, per-side current/previous counts, and an explicit Show previous feedback switch that reveals immutable earlier-RAG comments. Existing exact-node UUID and inherited top-level RAG data behavior remains unchanged and tested; final visual acceptance remains with the user.

tasks.title: Simplify the internal review landing page
tasks.description: Replace the oversized, promotional landing-page treatment with a compact and functional internal-tool layout that prioritizes finding and opening a paper.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing page no longer uses the massive multi-line hero title or marketing-style slogan treatment; the application identity and short purpose remain available in a compact header.

Paper collection navigation, search, results, and repository connection status become the primary above-the-fold content, with the paper browser visible without scrolling past a large introduction on a typical laptop viewport.

Decorative treatments that do not support review work—including excessive display typography, dramatic spacing, notebook-style background effects, heavy shadows, and dark showcase panels—are removed or substantially toned down.
The simplified landing page follows T10's light neutral palette and readable typography while retaining clear selected, hover, focus, invalid-source, empty, and disconnected states.

All existing landing-page behavior remains intact: live collection counts, collection selection, paper search, source details, invalid-paper handling, repository diagnostics, and navigation to stable paper routes.
The layout remains straightforward and usable at narrow and wide viewport sizes, with no decorative element taking priority over paper selection.
Browser tests preserve the landing-page browsing behavior, and visual verification at desktop and narrow widths confirms a compact internal-tool hierarchy rather than a promotional hero page.
tasks.notes: Fifth follow-up gap reported during user acceptance on 2026-09-06. Implemented on 2026-09-06 with a compact Choose a paper heading, short purpose copy, substantially reduced spacing and type scale, no ruled-paper background or showcase shadow, and a light collection rail so the paper browser is the primary content. The landing contract and production route smoke pass; final visual acceptance remains with the user.

tasks.title: Match the RTQ working hierarchy and section rail
tasks.description: Bring Review Content Web's rendered working area closer to the production RTQ website by restoring its labelled row hierarchy and rendering authored WorkingSection stages as a connected marker-and-rail sequence instead of flattening them into bare bold headings or rules.
acceptanceCriteria: The working area follows the production website's information hierarchy: tips use a Keep in mind row, formulas use a Formulas used row, the working body remains visually primary, and later working methods have a clear Method N separator.
Visible WorkingSection wrappers preserve their authored phase, optional title, body order, and boundaries in the prepared display model rather than being flattened into ordinary Markdown.

A sequence of visible WorkingSection stages renders with an understated left rail, per-stage marker, optional title rule, and terminal marker whose overall shape closely follows the production PaperViewWorkingSection treatment while fitting Review Content Web's light neutral theme.
Untitled stages retain the rail and body alignment without inventing a visible heading, and visibility=hidden stages remain hidden from the rendered view while staying available through Raw source.
Flat workings without WorkingSection wrappers continue to render normally and do not gain artificial stage headings or empty rail chrome.

The layout remains readable without overlap or clipped maths, tables, images, or raw-source disclosures at desktop and narrow widths, and formulas continue to appear before tips and the working body as previously required by the review site.

Preparation and interface tests cover structured, untitled, hidden, malformed, and flat working content plus the labelled rows, rail, and responsive styling; formatting, lint, types, tests, and production build pass.
tasks.notes: Follow-up requested during user acceptance on 2026-09-06. Implemented on 2026-09-06 using the production PaperViewWorking, PaperViewQuestionRowLabel, and PaperViewWorkingSection composition as the reference. Review Content Web now preserves WorkingSection stages as serializable display segments, hides visibility=hidden stages only from the rendered view, and renders visible stages with an untitled-aware marker, connected rail, optional title rule, and terminal marker. Formula and tip collections use Formulas used and Keep in mind rows, later methods use Method N dividers, and flat workings retain their ordinary rendering. Parser and static interface coverage pass alongside a production build and live structured-paper route inspection. Accepted by the user and marked done on 2026-09-06.

tasks.title: Add a whole-file macros review view
tasks.description: Expose the canonical rtq-content macros.toml as one dedicated read-only document in Review Content Web so reviewers can inspect every macro and its rendered expansion without treating it as a paper collection or enabling review mutations.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing-page collection rail contains a direct Macros link that remains distinct from TOML paper collections.
The macros route reads packages/papers/scripts/papers/lib/model/macros.toml directly from the active validated rtq-content checkout on every request.
Every parsed macro appears in source-file order with its identifier, macro category, and rendered Markdown/KaTeX expansion.
One sticky display setting expands or collapses the original source for every macro together, defaults to collapsed, and replaces the repeated per-macro disclosure controls.
A complete raw-file disclosure preserves comments and headings that are not represented by parsed TOML values.
The page uses the existing paper header and review typography but contains no review outcome, comment, tag-filter, or source-mutation controls.
Missing or invalid macro source fails safely with a reviewer-facing unavailable state, and model/interface coverage plus formatting, lint, types, tests, and production build pass.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-06 as the first read-only macro-review iteration. The new /macros route renders all 165 entries from the current 781-line canonical file and is linked from a Reference section in the landing-page collection rail. A follow-up replaces the 165 individual source disclosures with one sticky Show original source setting that reveals or hides every entry's source together; the separate complete-file raw disclosure remains available for comments and headings. The route reads only through the review-paper-model server boundary and deliberately omits all review and mutation plumbing. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Show newest review comments first
tasks.description: Present append-only review feedback in reverse chronological order so the latest comment is immediately visible at the top of both current-state and previous-state comment lists.
acceptanceCriteria: Current-RAG comments are displayed newest first using their stored created_at timestamps.
When previous feedback is enabled, historical-RAG comments are also displayed newest first.
Comment persistence remains append-only and stored rows and timestamps are not modified or migrated.
Ordering is deterministic when timestamps are equal, and automated coverage verifies unordered input with multiple current and historical comments.
Formatting, lint, types, tests, and the Review Content Web production build pass.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-06 by reversing the presentation-layer comment ordering in partitionReviewComments. Both current and historical groups now inherit the same newest-first ordering without changing SQLite retrieval or append-only storage. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Prevent comment focus from scrolling the question
tasks.description: Stop focus within review controls from activating the enclosing question and causing the URL-driven question navigation effect to scroll the viewport away from the comment composer.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking or keyboard-focusing a comment input, outcome button, link, toggle, or any other interactive descendant does not change the active-question URL or scroll the viewport to the top of the question.
Focusing the top-level question card itself can still activate it for keyboard navigation, and explicit previous/next question navigation retains its existing scroll behavior.
The fix applies to top-level questions, subquestions, and sub-subquestions without changing comment identity, RAG-state handling, or persistence.
Automated interface coverage guards the focus-target boundary, and formatting, lint, types, tests, and the Review Content Web production build pass.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-06 after tracing the jump to the question article's bubbling focus handler. The handler now activates only when the article itself receives focus; focus originating from a nested comment or review control is ignored. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Show the complete all-topics paper collection
tasks.description: Correct the generated collection registration from the nonexistent allTagsToml directory to the canonical rtq-content allTopicsToml projection so Review Content Web and Tag Web expose every generated all-topic paper.
acceptanceCriteria: Review Content Web discovers allTopicsToml directly from the configured rtq-content checkout and lists all eligible TOML papers in that folder after refresh.
All-topics filenames are interpreted as topic projections, producing a readable topic title and topic metadata rather than exposing the raw topicpapers filename.
Tag Web also discovers allTopicsToml and keeps the entire collection read-only; no tag mutation route accepts it as editable.
The nonexistent allTagsToml identifier is removed from maintained application code, tests, and documentation.
Collection fixtures cover discovery, topic metadata, source-path resolution, and Tag Web's read-only boundary; formatting, lint, types, tests, and affected production builds pass.
tasks.notes: Reported and corrected on 2026-09-06. The active content checkout contains 399 TOML papers in packages/papers/papers/allTopicsToml, while the review apps had registered allTagsToml, a directory that does not exist. Both apps now use the documented allTopicsToml name, with the collection remaining read-only in Tag Web. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Version the review-comment database in rtq-review
tasks.description: Resolve Review Content Web's Drizzle SQLite database from the rtq-review workspace instead of rtq-content so the checked-in feedback database is available for read-only use on other machines.
acceptanceCriteria: The default database path is <rtq-review>/database/review-content.sqlite and does not vary with RTQ_CONTENT_ROOT or the process working directory.
The existing tracked database file is preserved without copying from or modifying the former rtq-content database.
The main SQLite database remains tracked while review-content.sqlite-journal, review-content.sqlite-wal, and review-content.sqlite-shm remain ignored.
The application continues to use Drizzle for migration, listing, and append-only comment writes, with temporary-database tests isolated from the tracked database.
Documentation and automated repository checks describe and enforce the new versioned database boundary; formatting, lint, types, tests, and the production build pass.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-07. The user had already committed database/review-content.sqlite in rtq-review; the runtime now resolves that exact file through REVIEW_WORKSPACE_ROOT. No database content was copied or rewritten. The repository check now requires the main file to be tracked and not ignored while requiring only SQLite sidecars to be ignored. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Add simple review controls and outcome reset
tasks.description: Add a persistent simple-versus-advanced review mode, with an intentionally prominent Approved action and a Reset action that clears only the Google Sheets review outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: The sticky paper settings include a simple review switch whose selection survives refreshes in versioned local storage and defaults to the simple mode for new and migrated users.
Simple mode exposes exactly Approved and Reset as review-outcome actions for each top-level question and answer scope; Approved submits PRG and Reset submits an explicit empty outcome.
Advanced mode preserves all existing review-outcome actions and remains available without changing the SQLite feedback composer or history.
The Next.js mutation boundary represents Reset as null, while its Review API adapter sends an empty rag string; arbitrary empty strings remain invalid at the browser-facing boundary.
Review API permits an empty rag only as a reset after its existing UUID, sheet, and content-state validation, while continuing to allowlist every nonempty outcome.
Successful approval, reset, and comment submissions produce a bold high-contrast confirmation and a visibly green review scope.
Automated coverage verifies preference migration, both modes, reset forwarding, and the preserved advanced outcome set; app and API checks pass without contacting Google Sheets.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-07. Reset clears the Google Sheets outcome cell only; append-only SQLite feedback is deliberately unaffected. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Add filter-aware hierarchical question navigation
tasks.description: Replace the section-only paper rail with a simple sticky hierarchy that links directly to every visible question, subquestion, and sub-subquestion.
acceptanceCriteria: The left rail shows the section and complete displayed hierarchy of top-level questions, subquestions, and sub-subquestions.
Every node link targets that exact rendered node and jumps directly to its existing stable question anchor.
The rail is derived from matchingSections, so dimensional-tag, question-RAG, answer-RAG, and cleared-filter states update the rail and paper from the same result.
Exact matching nodes are visually distinguished from retained context nodes, without hiding descendants that remain visible in the matching question tree.
The rail remains available in a compact non-sticky form on narrow screens and avoids animation-specific behavior.
Automated interface coverage verifies recursion, filtered input, exact-node anchors, and sticky desktop presentation.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-07 using the existing filtered matchingSections tree, avoiding a second navigation-specific filtering model. Awaiting user review.

tasks.title: Remove repeated hidden-feedback prompts
tasks.description: Remove the per-review-scope message that repeats how many previous comments are hidden, while retaining the single global Show previous feedback control and the actual historical feedback view.
acceptanceCriteria: No question, subquestion, sub-subquestion, question-side scope, or answer-side scope renders the repeated hidden-comments instruction.
The sticky Show previous feedback setting remains the only control for revealing history and continues to show immutable earlier-state comments when enabled.
Current and previous counts remain available in the feedback heading without an additional instructional paragraph.
Automated interface coverage guards both removal of the repeated prompt and retention of the global control.
tasks.notes: Requested and implemented on 2026-09-07 to reduce repeated noise on mixed-RAG papers. Awaiting user review.

validation: Run the renamed review-markdown-web application's existing format, lint, type, test, and build checks through its new package identity
Load the rtq-content tmux review-stack configuration and smoke-check review-content-web on port 3001, review-markdown-web on port 3004, and docs-web on port 3005
Verify the tracked rtq-review database and ignored SQLite sidecars, and ensure functional changes to existing apps and user-owned Gatsby changes remain untouched
openQuestions: Confirm that initial collection support should follow the documented paper-level registry plus discovered exemplar levels, rather than automatically treating every future *Toml directory as a compatible paper collection.
Confirm exact-match filters with OR within one dimension and AND between dimensions; hierarchical prefix matching such as math.number including math.number.fraction is not currently assumed.
Confirm that a descendant match includes the complete top-level question tree for context and highlights matching nodes, rather than removing nonmatching siblings inside that tree.
Determine reviewer identity behavior; current maintained UI code hard-codes up, while the new app could use one explicit environment setting or a local reviewer selector.
Confirm whether automatic selected-file refresh is required or whether a visible stale indicator plus manual refresh is sufficient during the first iteration.
Decide whether a later iteration should construct virtual cross-paper result sets directly from canonical TOML so topic and RAG derived files become optional for review browsing.
decisions: Build a new Next.js application in rtq-review rather than changing an existing review website.
Rename the existing generated-Markdown Next.js application from review-web to review-markdown-web while preserving its behavior.
Name the new direct-TOML application review-content-web and run it as the primary reviewer on port 3001.
Update the rtq-content-owned tmux YAML in this delivery so the primary review-content-web starts on port 3001, review-markdown-web moves to port 3004, and docs-web moves to port 3005.
Keep every existing review application operational and exclude the legacy Gatsby application from design and reuse analysis.
Read TOML and maths assets directly from the active rtq-content checkout at runtime; generated Markdown is not an input.
Treat all paper content as read-only while retaining question-side and answer-side review outcome writes through review-api to Google Sheets.

Persist new question-side and answer-side comments only through Drizzle in the tracked <rtq-review>/database/review-content.sqlite file. Each node is keyed by its own UUID and own question ID when present; nested nodes inherit only the corresponding top-level RAG state and never the parent's identity. History is append-only with no reset or delete behavior.
Version the main SQLite database with rtq-review so feedback can be read on other machines, while keeping its journal, WAL, and SHM sidecars untracked.
Show exact-current-state comments as active feedback by default; expose immutable comments from other RAG states only through a page-level Show everything toggle.
Use dimensional tags as runtime filter facets and support combining tags from different dimensions.
Preserve canonical TOML as the complete-paper source of truth and treat generated TOML folders as replaceable projections.
Use review-tag-web as the primary reference for collection browsing, complete-paper parsing, tag inheritance, assets, and paper navigation.
Use review-question-viewer-web as the primary reference for a structured raw/rendered content model and React-based review controls.
Use review-markdown-web as the behavioral reference for bulk review, display preferences, and review action coverage, but do not reuse its generated-Markdown DOM mutation architecture.
Do not modify review-api for local comment persistence; its outcome endpoints remain the Google Sheets boundary, and its legacy comment endpoints remain available only to existing applications.

Represent outcome reset as null inside Review Content Web and translate it to an empty Review API rag value that clears the validated Google Sheets outcome cell; never delete or reset SQLite feedback.
notes: Code review completed against the maintained Next.js applications, review-api, @rtq/review-repository-paths, the canonical dimensional-tag documentation, the derived-TOML runbook, the paper-review process, and the RAG-state architecture. The two direct-TOML apps currently duplicate substantial parser/asset/tag logic and have drifted in macros, PaperTable handling, placeholder behavior, types, and test coverage. The new app should reconcile a tested superset behind its own read-only package boundary; migration of existing apps can be considered later as a separate risk-controlled task. The review-web to review-markdown-web rename is naming/configuration work only, while the rtq-content tmux update is an explicitly required cross-repository integration change rather than a deferred follow-up.
